model_definition.model_name: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) for lithium-ion battery SOH estimation
model_definition.architecture: The model takes extracted statistical features x and cycle/time t as inputs to estimate SOH. It consists of two neural-network-approximated components: a solution function f(·), implemented as neural network F(·), that maps cycle/features to SOH, and a nonlinear degradation-dynamics function g(·), implemented as neural network G(·), that models the SOH decay rate/degradation dynamics. The PINN is constrained by an empirical/state-space degradation equation expressed as a PDE, plus monotonic degradation behavior. During transfer learning, G(·) is frozen and only the solution component F(·) is fine-tuned.

layers.purpose: Models nonlinear battery SOH decay rate / degradation dynamics

loss_terms.name: PDE/degradation-equation loss

model_definition.training_paradigm: Physics-informed supervised learning using labeled SOH data plus degradation-dynamics constraints; small-sample learning experiments are conducted; transfer learning uses source-domain pretraining followed by target-domain fine-tuning with G(·) frozen and F(·) fine-tuned.

evidence.text: The paper states that the proposed method is a PINN for battery SOH estimation belonging to the B2 architecture, integrating governing equations and neural networks, modeling degradation dynamics from empirical degradation and state-space equations.

The framework description states that the proposed PINN consists of a solution function f(·) mapping features to SOH and a nonlinear function g(·) modeling battery degradation dynamics; f(·) and g(·) are replaced by small fully connected neural networks F(·) and G(·).
The training losses are described as data term loss L_data, monotonicity loss L_mono, and PDE loss L_PDE constrained by the degradation equation.

The feature extraction method extracts mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, skewness, charging time, accumulated charge, curve slope, and curve entropy from selected current and voltage curves, giving 16 features.
The SOH estimation section states that the extracted 16 features and time/cycle are used as inputs of the proposed PINN and that min–max normalization scales features to [-1,1].
The fine-tuning section states that degradation dynamics are treated as general, G is frozen, and only the solution component is fine-tuned for transfer learning.

experiment_protocol.train_val_test_split: For regular SOH estimation experiments, each dataset was split into training batteries, validation batteries, and test batteries approximately at a 6:2:2 ratio. The number of test batteries was reported in supplementary Table S2, and test batteries were distributed evenly throughout each dataset. For small-sample experiments, the authors trained with 1, 2, 3, or 4 batteries and tested on the same test set as the regular SOH estimation experiment.
experiment_protocol.cross_validation: No k-fold cross-validation is described. Instead, model training and testing were repeated 10 times for each model/dataset setting, and reported values were averaged across ten experiments.
experiment_protocol.train_test_by_battery_or_random: Splitting was by battery/cell, not random samples: the paper states that training batteries, validation batteries, and test batteries were divided approximately 6:2:2. Small-sample experiments also used whole battery data for training and multiple held-out batteries for testing.
experiment_protocol.transfer_setting: Transfer learning was evaluated using pairwise fine-tuning among four datasets. A PINN was first trained on a source-domain dataset, then fine-tuned using data from the 1st battery in the target-domain dataset, and tested on the target-domain test set. During transfer, the degradation-dynamics network G was frozen and only the solution/mapping network was fine-tuned. Source-only experiments trained on the source domain and directly tested on the target-domain test set without fine-tuning. These were compared against models trained directly with 1 or 2 target-domain batteries. For transfer table convenience, XJTU batch 1 represented XJTU and TJU batch 3 represented TJU.

evaluation_flow: Collect/use four large-scale datasets totaling 387 batteries and 310,705 samples.

For each cycle/sample, extract statistical features from a short period before the battery is fully charged: voltage data in [V_end - 0.2, V_end] and current data between 0.5 A and 0.1 A during constant-voltage charging.

Extract 16 features from selected current and voltage curves: mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, skewness, charging time, accumulated charge, curve slope, and curve entropy for current and voltage respectively.
Use the 16 extracted features plus time/cycle as inputs to estimate SOH.
Apply min–max normalization to scale all features to [-1, 1].
Train the proposed PINN using losses including data-term loss, monotonicity loss, and PDE/degradation-equation-constrained loss.
Compare against MLP with the same structure/parameter amount and CNN with similar parameter amount.
Regular experiments: split each dataset by batteries into train/validation/test sets at approximately 6:2:2 and evaluate SOH estimation on held-out test batteries.
Repeat training/testing 10 times per model/dataset to assess mean performance and stability.
Report MAPE and RMSE in tables; MAE, MAPE, and RMSE distributions are shown for repeated experiments.
Small-sample experiments: train PINN, MLP, and CNN using 1, 2, 3, or 4 batteries, then test on the same held-out test set as the regular experiment; evaluate primarily with MAPE and RMSE.
Transfer experiments: train PINN on source dataset, freeze dynamics network G, fine-tune only the solution network using the 1st battery from target dataset, and test on the target-domain test set.
Transfer baselines: source-only direct testing on target without fine-tuning, and training directly with 1 or 2 target-domain batteries.

architectures.model_name: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) for battery SOH estimation

layers.details: Extracted 16 statistical features plus time/cycle are used as model inputs; features are min-max normalized to [-1, 1].

The PINN consists of two neural-network-approximated functions: a solution function F(·) mapping features and cycle/time to SOH, and a nonlinear dynamics function G(·) modeling battery degradation/SOH decay dynamics.
Training uses data loss, monotonicity loss, and PDE/degradation-equation loss so predictions match true SOH while satisfying monotonic degradation and the established degradation model.
